segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, for -ar verbs we have -amos in the present for we.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Now, for -er verbs we have -emos for the we, and for -ir verbs we have -imos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: This is the only time in the whole language that we find a difference between -er and -ir verbs. They're one group.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: But here, and it's the only time in the entire language, we have a difference between the two of them in the present for we. For -ir verbs we have -imos, and for -er verbs we have -emos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, preferir, what do you think that means, preferir?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. To prefer. To prefer. We want to think with the "to". Whenever the verb ends in an "r", it's going to help us just to think of that as "to". To prefer, preferir.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So how would you say, I prefer?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. How would you say, we prefer? And preferir has an -ir ending.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Preferimos. So there the "e" doesn't split, and also the "i" of -ir is appearing in the endings for the first time in the present tense. Preferimos. Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Had something to do with convenient, when things "with come".

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Venir. And how would you say, we come, or we're coming?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: To live in Spanish is vivir. V-I-V-I-R, vivir.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: You might know this from "¡Viva la Revolución!", you might have heard that somewhere, "long live the revolution", "¡Viva la Revolución!" Or you might have even heard "¡Viva Las Vegas!" Long live Las Vegas. Vivir, to live.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How do you say, I live?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Here in Spanish is "aquí" or "acá". "Aquí" in Spain and "acá" in Latin America. Everybody understands both. It's an extremely common word, so you don't have to worry. "Aquí" or "acá".

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. But he lives here, and let's stress that because we're contrasting, but he lives here?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Let's make it all together. I don't live here, but he lives here.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: No vivo aquí, pero él vive aquí.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. And don't be afraid to try the soft "b". If it's too difficult, then it's not a problem that you pronounce the "v". You maybe want to pronounce the "v" at the beginning and then see what happens. But the more you pronounce like how people are speaking around you, the more you understand.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Saber. This is a "b" (Student: It's a "b", saber), saber, this is a "b". So you're not going to pronounce a "v", saber.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So we have vivir, to live. We need to open up that association of the letter "v" to include that soft "b". Maybe you look up the word in the dictionary for summer, which is "verano" or "berano". Now if you just program your mind with "verano", maybe you won't get it when you hear "berano".

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So it always makes sense to pronounce the words the way people around you are pronouncing. So if you are practicing Spanish with Colombians, take their accent. If you are practicing with people from Río de la Plata, Buenos Aires, Montevideo, who have kind of particular accent, take that accent as well. If you're practicing with people from Madrid, take their accent. The more you speak like the people you're listening to, the easier you understand.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Vivimos. There we have the "i" popping up, vivimos. But for the other versions, we're going to have the "e". So he lives?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Some vowel harmony you're making there? Vivir. The "e" is correct, but you changed the beginning to match that "e".

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Vive. Before you said debe (Student: [laughs] Ah!). It's vowel harmony again. So you must consciously take off that ending, see what you're left with, vivir, viv-, and put on your "e", vive. Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: The word for where is dónde, dónde. So how would you say, where do they live?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: I want to know where they live.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Quiero saber dónde viven. Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Entender, entender, is to understand, entender. We said we can use comprender as well, which might be easy to remember, but entender is much more common. How do you say, I understand?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Entiendo. Good, the "e" splits. Entender, entiendo. He understands?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: ¿Por qué no entiende? Good. I want to know why he doesn't understand.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Quiero saber por qué no entiende.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Quiero saber por qué no entiende. Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How do you think you would say, we understand?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. So for -er verbs we have -emos. So this is the only difference in the entire language, huh, between -er verbs and -ir verbs. For everything else, they are exactly the same. But for we in the present tense, we get -imos and -emos. Vivir, vivimos; venir, venimos; preferir, preferimos. And then for -er verbs, -emos: entender, entendemos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Perder, which we said was to lose, so how do you say, we lose?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: The word for always in Spanish is siempre, siempre. So how would you say, we always lose?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And there you can put the "siempre" before or afterwards.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Siempre perdemos. We always lose, or perdemos siempre.
